title: Three Months and One Short Stamp
subtitle: 国家公民 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）
meta: 主题语境：国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）　|　核心词汇：nationality　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 nationality 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1976 the clerk ① stated the nationality that no applicant in the office would have counted, and he said the stating was the whole of the month. The ② nationality, meaning the status itself and not the stamp, ran three months and stayed uncounted in the book; a nationality, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ nationality in that office had the same short stamp beside it, and the ④ nationality at the far counter, meaning the form they kept for the children to sign and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A nationality, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the clerk said the counting is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the nationality was the whole of the matter, meaning the belonging and not the status. The ⑥ nationality, meaning the belonging and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; nationality, he said, is either something you state or the only word that means both a status and a belonging. He said the belonging is the part they remember.

By 1981 the ⑦ nationality had become a line in a file, and the file had become an argument about the short stamp. The ⑧ nationality of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in May, was one office and three months of counting; nationality, he said, is either the form at the far counter or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ nationality I remember is the status counted in the file, which closed in 1983 and is still counted as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ nationality, my mother said in 1985, is the only status that improves by being counted; every nationality, she said, is a belonging that has agreed to look like a status. She said the belonging was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 国籍；民族（指办事处里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 国籍；民族（指那个国籍本身，与小小的印章相对）
C. 固定搭配：state the nationality 填报这一个国籍
D. n. 国籍；民族（指留给孩子们签的那一份）
E. n. 国籍之事（抽象总称，指一处办事处的国籍之事）
F. n. 国籍；民族（指卷宗里写到、被清点的那一个）
G. n. 国籍、归属（指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 归属（抽象总称，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: stated the nationality that no applicant in the office would have counted

answers.why: state the nationality 意为“填报这一个国籍”，1976 年那位书记员把办事处里没有一位申请人肯清点的一个国籍做了一遍。
nationality 意为“国籍；民族”，指那个国籍本身而不是小小的印章，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被清点。
nationality 意为“国籍；民族”，指办事处里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一枚小小的印章。
nationality 意为“国籍；民族”，指最远那个窗口的留给孩子们签的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
nationality 意为“国籍、归属”，指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个归属就是那件事的全部。
nationality 意为“归属”，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个国籍，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
nationality 意为“国籍；民族”，指卷宗里写到、被清点的那一个，到 1981 年这一个成了卷宗里的一行。
nationality 意为“国籍之事”，书记员五月写道，整件事的国籍之事是一处办事处和三个月份的清点。
nationality 意为“国籍；民族”，我记得的是卷宗里清点过的那一个，1983 年办结了，至今仍被说成办事处里最安静的一个。
nationality 为抽象总称，母亲 1985 年说，国籍是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的国籍。

那个国籍，指的是那个国籍本身而不是小小的印章，经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被清点。（nationality）
那处办事处里每一个国籍旁边都有同一枚小小的印章。（nationality）

叔叔说这个归属就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那个国籍。（nationality）
